first.rationale: Current situation shows two concurrent headwinds: competitive price pressure on SMB and declining activation/onboarding metrics. Memory_73 documents that targeted promotional pricing is effective for price-sensitive SMB segments with acquisition and revenue lift. Memory_31 on signup simplification and memory_86 on onboarding shortening address the activation decline, but onboarding simplification is lower-risk for retention given we have limited verification capacity and don't yet know if the 4% completion decline is driven by friction or other factors. Promotional pricing directly addresses the immediate competitive threat while we can separately observe activation trends. We verify memory_73 (promotional pricing efficacy) and memory_31 (simplification lift) to confirm the pricing lever is sound and to rule out that signup friction is the primary activation driver before committing one experiment slot to pricing. A small guarded test (cohort-based, limited audience) preserves optionality and avoids broad exposure to margin risk if competitive pricing proves unsustainable. Memory_57 (referral performance in established base) is noted but referral incentives don't address the new-customer competitive pressure. This preserves uncertainty about root causes of the activation decline while acting on the clearest immediate threat.

final.rationale: Archive review reveals critical constraint: memory_73 (promotional pricing) shows -12% 30-day retention on the acquired cohort and does not survive renewal. This disqualifies promotional_pricing despite short-term acquisition lift, as it directly conflicts with the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Memory_31 confirms signup simplification works for SMB activation (+9% activation, +4% qualified revenue, only -1% retention risk). The current activation decline (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion decline (4% QoQ) suggest activation messaging and/or onboarding friction are primary drivers. Memory_91 shows in-product activation messaging improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to first meaningful action—directly addressing the activation headwind. Memory_86 confirms onboarding shortening lifted adoption. Activation_messaging targets the immediate 6% activation decline with proven mechanism (memory_91) and minimal retention risk, while preserving the option to layer signup simplification or onboarding optimization later. This addresses the non-price competitive threat (customer success and time-to-value) and avoids the retention cliff documented in exp_73. Standard_experiment scope allows confident signal detection on a 1-week timeline.
